speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are presenting with gait and limb ataxia; to begin my assessment, could you please describe when these symptoms first started and if they have been getting worse over time? You also mentioned a significant medical history; please detail your past diagnoses and any relevant surgeries or family history of neurological conditions.

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds concerning; could you clarify if your ataxia is constant or if it improves when you sleep, and do you experience any numbness or weakness in your limbs? Additionally, are you currently taking any medications or supplements?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy. The patient's history of Crohn's disease treated with natalizumab, combined with new-onset asymmetric gait and limb ataxia, is highly suspicious for JC virus reactivation. I request an MRI of the brain to confirm the presence of non-enhancing white matter lesions typical of PML.
